According to recent reports, the S&P 500 is an index that tracks the 500 largest publicly traded companies in the United States, weighted by market capitalization. It includes Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Nvidia, Alphabet (Google), Meta, Berkshire Hathaway, and approximately 493 other companies that collectively represent about 80% of the total U.S. stock market value.

Industry observers note that the index is maintained by S&P Dow Jones Indices, which periodically adds and removes companies based on criteria including market cap (must exceed ~$18 billion), profitability, liquidity, and domicile. When a company is added to the S&P 500, every index fund tracking it automatically buys shares — and vice versa when companies are removed.

An S&P 500 index fund is a mutual fund or exchange-traded fund (ETF) that holds all 500 stocks in the same proportions as the index. Instead of picking individual stocks, you buy one fund and instantly own a piece of every major U.S. company. The fund mechanically replicates the index — no stock picking, no market timing, no overpaid fund managers.

Recent findings suggest that the data is overwhelming. Over any 15-year period, approximately 92% of actively managed large-cap funds underperform the S&P 500 after fees, according to the SPIVA scorecard. Over 20 years, that number exceeds 95%. The reasons are simple: active fund managers charge 0.50% to 1.50% in annual fees, they generate taxable trading activity, and they cannot consistently pick winners.

Warren Buffett bet $1 million that an S&P 500 index fund would beat a selection of hedge funds over 10 years. He won decisively — the index fund returned 125.8% vs 36.0% for the hedge fund basket. As Buffett has remarked: "By periodically investing in an index fund, the know-nothing investor can actually outperform most investment professionals.".

Recent findings suggest that the top S&P 500 index funds deliver nearly identical performance because they all track the same index. The differences come down to expense ratio, minimum investment, fund structure (ETF vs mutual fund), and tax efficiency. Here is a detailed comparison of the five most popular options.

The most popular S&P 500 ETF and the default recommendation for most FI seekers. At 0.03% expense ratio, a $500,000 investment costs just $150 per year in fees. VOO is tax-efficient due to the ETF structure and Vanguard's patented heartbeat trade process, which minimizes capital gains distributions. Fractional shares are available at most brokerages.

Recent findings suggest that the lowest-cost S&P 500 fund available at 0.015% — half the cost of VOO. No minimum investment requirement makes it ideal for beginners. As a mutual fund, you can set up automatic investments in exact dollar amounts (e.g., $500/month). FXAIX is an excellent choice if your brokerage is Fidelity.

In a recent development, blackRock's S&P 500 ETF with a 0.03% expense ratio, matching VOO. Functionally identical performance. Slightly different creation/redemption mechanics than VOO but the practical difference for individual investors is negligible. A strong alternative if you prefer iShares or trade through a brokerage that offers commission-free iShares ETFs.

The oldest and most heavily traded S&P 500 ETF, launched in 1993. SPY is the most liquid ETF in the world, making it the preferred choice for active traders. However, its 0.0945% expense ratio is over three times higher than VOO or IVV. For long-term FI investors, VOO or IVV are better choices. SPY's structure as a unit investment trust also makes it slightly less tax-efficient than VOO.

Industry observers note that schwab's mutual fund offering at 0.02% expense ratio with no minimum investment. Like FXAIX, the mutual fund structure allows automatic dollar-amount investing. An excellent choice for Schwab customers building automated investment intends.

Investing in an S&P 500 fund takes less than 15 minutes:.

For retirement accounts (401k, IRA), look for the S&P 500 index fund option within your blueprint. It may have a different name (e.g., "Large Cap Index Fund" or "Institutional S&P 500") but will track the same index.

The total stock market index (tracked by VTI/VTSAX/FSKAX) holds approximately 3,600 stocks compared to the S&P 500's 500. The additional 3,100 stocks are mid-cap and small-cap companies. Here is how they compare:.

Historically, the performance difference between the two is minimal — typically within 0.1-0.3% per year in either direction. The S&P 500 has outperformed in periods when large-cap growth stocks dominate. The total market has outperformed when small and mid-cap stocks lead. Over 20+ year periods, the returns converge closely.

According to recent reports, the FI community's honest answer: it does not matter much which you choose. Investing $25,500 per year in VOO or VTI will produce nearly identical outcomes over 20 years. Consistency and contribution amount matter far more than the choice between S&P 500 and total market.

Recent findings suggest that S&P 500 index funds typically yield 1.2% to 1.6% in annual dividends. In a tax-advantaged account (401k, IRA, Roth), dividends compound tax-free. In a taxable account, qualified dividends from S&P 500 funds are taxed at the favorable long-term capital gains rate (0%, 15%, or 20% depending on income).

Sources indicate that ETFs (VOO, IVV) are generally more tax-efficient than mutual funds (FXAIX, SWPPX) in taxable accounts because ETFs rarely distribute capital gains. Vanguard's mutual funds are an exception — their patented ETF share class structure gives Vanguard mutual funds ETF-like tax efficiency. For taxable brokerage accounts, VOO or VFIAX (Vanguard's mutual fund version) are the most tax-efficient choices.

Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.

The most common mistake with S&P 500 index funds is waiting for the "right time" to invest. Research from Vanguard shows that investing a lump sum immediately outperforms dollar-cost averaging about two-thirds of the time, because markets go up more often than they go down. Missing just the 10 best trading days over a 20-year period can cut your returns nearly in half. If you have money to invest, the data overwhelmingly says to invest it now — not next week, not after the next pullback, not when it "feels right.".

Sources indicate that open an account at Vanguard (for VOO/VFIAX), Fidelity (for FXAIX), or Schwab (for SWPPX). All three offer commission-free trading on their own index funds, excellent customer service, and robust retirement account options. You can also buy any of these funds at most brokerages.

ETFs (VOO, IVV) trade like stocks at real-time prices and are more tax-efficient in taxable accounts. Mutual funds (FXAIX, SWPPX) allow automatic dollar-amount investing and are better for set-it-and-forget-it contribution schedules. For retirement accounts, either works equally well.

Sources indicate that transfer cash to your brokerage account and buy your chosen fund. Start with whatever you have — there is no minimum too small. FXAIX and SWPPX have $0 minimums, and VOO can be purchased in fractional shares at most brokerages for as little as $1.

Recent findings suggest that automate monthly or per-paycheck contributions. This removes emotion from the process and ensures consistent dollar-cost averaging. Most brokerages let you schedule recurring purchases of mutual funds. For ETFs, some brokerages offer automatic ETF purchases as well.

Sources indicate that if you hold other asset classes (bonds, international), rebalance once per year to maintain your target allocation. Otherwise, do nothing — do not check daily prices, do not sell during downturns, and do not chase performance. The S&P 500 has recovered from every crash in history. Time in the market beats timing the market.

Fidelity 500 Index Fund (FXAIX) has the lowest expense ratio at 0.015%. Schwab S&P 500 Index Fund (SWPPX) is next at 0.02%. VOO and IVV tie at 0.03%. All four are excellent — the fee difference between FXAIX (0.015%) and VOO (0.03%) on a $500,000 portfolio is just $75 per year. Choose the fund offered by your preferred brokerage.

VOO is better for long-term investors. It charges 0.03% vs SPY's 0.0945%, saving you about $325 per year on a $500,000 portfolio. VOO is also more tax-efficient due to its ETF share class structure. SPY's advantage is liquidity for active trading, which long-term index investors do not need. For buy-and-hold FI investing, VOO is the clear winner.

In a recent development, either is an excellent choice. The S&P 500 covers approximately 80% of the U.S. stock market by value. A total market fund adds mid-cap and small-cap stocks for fuller diversification. Over long periods, performance is nearly identical — typically within 0.1-0.3% per year. The FI community consensus is that the best fund is the one you will consistently invest in without overthinking the decision.

According to recent reports, as little as $1. FXAIX and SWPPX have zero minimum investments. VOO and IVV can be purchased as fractional shares at most brokerages. There is no minimum too small — starting with $50 or $100 per month and increasing contributions as your income grows is exactly how most people on the FI path begin.

The S&P 500 has returned approximately 10.3% per year on average since 1957 (including dividends). Adjusted for inflation, the real return is approximately 7.0% per year. These are long-term averages — individual years range from -38% (2008) to +38% (1995). The key is staying invested through the down years to capture the recovery gains that follow.

Recent findings suggest that S&P 500 index funds carry market risk — they can lose significant value in the short term (the index dropped 34% in early 2020 and 38% in 2008). However, the S&P 500 has recovered from every decline in its history and has never lost money over any 20-year period. For investors with a 10+ year time horizon, the risk of not investing (missing out on 10% average annual returns) is far greater than the risk of temporary market declines.

Sources indicate that S&P 500 index funds are the single most vital building block for long-term wealth. With expense ratios as low as 0.015%, you keep virtually all of your returns while owning a piece of the 500 largest U.S. companies. VOO, FXAIX, IVV, and SWPPX all deliver near-identical performance — choose the fund offered by your preferred brokerage and automate your contributions. The FI community has proven through thousands of real-world examples that consistent investing in a low-cost S&P 500 index fund, held for decades without panic selling, is the most reliable path to building wealth and reaching financial independence.

Latest Update: Save Major Without Sacrificing Comfort With These Editor-Tested Running Shoes Under $130

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that we earn a commission for products purchased through some links in this article.
  • Editor’s Note, November 19, 2026: Black Friday sales are in full swing.
  • “All you need is a pair of shoes to start running” isn’t exactly truthful.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that we earn a commission for products purchased through some links in this article. Why Trust Us?

Editor’s Note, November 19, 2026: Black Friday sales are in full swing. Several of our already low-priced trainers are discounted for as high as 30% off, including our Best Overall, the New Balance 680v9.

“All you need is a pair of shoes to start running” isn’t exactly truthful. If you hate your toenails and heels, by all means, wear Converse high-tops. A good pair of running shoes will spare your digits and the skin on your feet—but that doesn’t mean you have to drop cash on expensive trainers.

Cheap running shoes, models less than $130, are a respectable choice for beginners and vets wanting to save. From plush to moderately cushioned, we’ve listed affordable running shoes on this list that’ll help you save up for more run gear, like a fancy GPS watch or that next destination race.

To find the best shoes under $130, we performed comprehensive research on top-rated trainers by well-known brands, and called in shoes for our shoe program testers and staff to evaluate. These shoes were vetted by scrutinizing fit, ride, and comfort. To give you both options, we included our premium recommendation for each shoe from our Best Running Shoes buying guide, just in case you want to spend some extra cash.

🏃 For even more choices, head to The Best Running Shoes of 2026.

We also spoke with Footwear Buyer Jon Notary, who works at the local running store Aardvark Sports Shop in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania. Notary provides insight on what you’re compromising on when buying cheap shoes, and gives advice on what to look for when you’re out shopping for your next pair.

Buying an affordable trainer doesn’t necessarily mean subpar features. Brands will sometimes incorporate “old” technology into these shoes, like midsole foams, to mitigate a high price. But you are sacrificing some premium specs, like plush cushioning and more durable materials.

Below is a comparison chart of our Best Overall budget trainer, the New Balance Fresh Foam 680v9, versus the brand’s premium daily trainer, the Fresh Foam X 880v15. The latter has the next generation of Fresh Foam, Fresh Foam X, and more cushioning. You save almost half the money with the 680v9, but you get what you paid for with the 880v15.

The 680v9 is still a reliable shoe for everyday runs and light workouts. If you’re an efficient runner (you don’t wear down your shoes’ soles faster than the average runner), you may even get more mileage out of the 680v9s. It comes down to what you’re willing to give up and what you’re willing to spend.

Recent findings suggest that all the trainers on this list are Best Value material, but the 680v9 deserves the title for its consistency with each upgrade. Though not as plush or responsive as, say, the more expensive 1080 or 880, the 680 still encapsulates New Balance’s soft-cushioned feel, absorbing shock and promoting comfort on every run.

Its Fresh Foam midsole provides a supportive, plush, lightweight ride, making the 680v9 an excellent choice as an everyday trainer that can handle base-building mileage. A breathable, cozy upper makes this a comfy running shoe and great for casual wear, as well.

It has been revealed that 👟 Want to go premium? Try our Best Value Shoe → Newly introduced Balance Ellipse (Men’s/Women’s).

Shop Men’s at newbalance.com | Shop Women’s at newbalance.com.

Sources indicate that you can’t go wrong with the Launch 12 for a speed shoe, especially when it has DNA Flash v2, the foam featured in the Hyperion Elite 4. The nitrogen-infused supercritical foam is lightweight and responsive; it provides plenty of pop for fast workouts on the road and track.

One drawback, at least for runners with wide feet, is that the midfoot area is quite narrow.

In a recent development, “No matter how many times I loosened and re-laced my shoes, it always felt too tight through the midfoot area, causing some noticeable discomfort,” said RW editor Ashley Tysiac. “While I can appreciate its secure fit, I think this system could have been reimagined to be a bit more forgiving in that area to provide more comfort.”.

Despite her distaste for the Launch 12’s tightness, she praised the shoe’s lightweight and responsiveness. Tysiac found the shoe’s simplicity refreshing in our max-cushioned era of trainers.

“I think the weight of the shoe is the best part, as it’s very light yet provides a pretty stable ride,” she said. “That made it the perfect shoe for runs where I wanted to pick up the pace a bit without being dragged down by heavy shoes, and even a good option for those recovery days when I still wanted to feel light on my feet while running at a slower pace.”.

In a recent development, 👟 Want to go premium? Try our Best Overall Shoe → Adidas Adizero Evo SL (Men’s/Women’s).

Shop Men’s at brooksrunning.com | Shop Women’s at brooksrunning.com.

According to recent reports, the GT-1000 15 provides stability without overbearing, rigid foam pieces, or a high price tag. The shoe has Asics’s 3D Guidance System, which uses a broader platform and reshaping in the heel and forefoot to help with inward foot rolling.

Sources indicate that the shoe has high-abrasion Ahar rubber that can withstand aggressive gait patterns and provide reliable traction on slippery surfaces and sharp corners. The fit is slightly narrower than past models, so you may want to size up.

The shoe is also great for long runs thanks to its PureGel tech and FF Blast midsole; you’ll have a soft ride that absorbs impact.

👟 Want to go premium? Try our Best Stability Shoe → Brooks Adrenaline GTS 26 (Men’s/Women’s).

Shop Men’s at amazon.com | Shop Women’s at amazon.com.

Industry observers note that the FloatZig 2 looks bulky with its unconventional, zigzag midsole rim around the shoe. But we found it surprisingly lightweight during testing. Its soft cushioning—that midsole isn’t just for looks—provided a supportive bed for testers’ feet.

“What I found most enjoyable about this shoe was how lightweight and balanced it is,” said tester Mike Parmer. “The fit and comfort allowed longer training runs and no sore feet or toes. This shoe is one of the better shoes I have tested recently and would compare equally to Hoka.”.

The Superfloat+ midsole promotes high energy return, giving a much-needed boost when the road feels long.

In a recent development, 👟 Want to go premium? Try our Best for Shock Absorption Shoe → New Balance 1080v15 (Men’s/Women’s).

Shop Men’s at reebok.com | Shop Women’s at reebok.com.

Anta proves you can have premium cushioning on a budget. The PG7 3 has an incredibly plush feel, making the shoe versatile for easy runs, long runs, and casual wear. The cushioning stays soft and also supportive, allowing you to run hard and fast.

In my runs in the PG7 3, I’ve found the ride and feel comparable to the Saucony Triumph and Brooks Glycerin.

According to recent reports, “Budget shoes always feel cheap,” said Runner-in-Chief Jeff Dengate. “There’s an undeniable compromise you have to make to pay less. And that stinks. In this case, the PG7 doesn’t really feel like it’s holding anything back. It’s comfortable, cushioned, and supportive. It’s going to work as a daily driver for a lot of runners.”.

It has been revealed that 👟 Want to go premium? Try our Best for Long Runs Shoe → Nike Structure Plus (Men’s/Women’s).

Shop Men’s at amazon.com | Shop Women’s at amazon.com.

According to recent reports, though the C202 7 costs the most on this list, it’s more than worth the $130 price. Compared to racing shoes that are upward of $200, the C202 7 has a full-length carbon-fiber plate sandwiched in its midsole of DAN cushioning, a TPU supercritical foam.

In a recent development, the shoe feels snappy and responsive. And it has good traction too. Furrer tested the shoe during a rainy 5K in San Antonio, Texas. While other competitors wiped out on slick turns, Furrer stayed vertical cutting corners and accelerating on waterlogged sidewalks and muddy dividers.

In a recent development, 👟 Want to go premium? Try our Best for Racing Marathons Shoe → Adidas Adizero Adios Pro 5 (Men’s/Women’s).

Trail running demands a lot from your shoes. Between the hard-charging descents and scraping against rough rocks, the last thing you want is a cheap, flimsy shoe that won’t hold up. The Saucony Excursion TR17 has Versarun, which absorbs impact and provides comfy cushioning over trail debris.

One knock is the shoe is quite heavy, and it runs a little small and narrow, so consider sizing up and trying on the wide version.

All models of the Excursion TR17 have 4.5mm lugs to keep you on your toes when things get dicey.

👟 Want to go premium? Try our Best for Trails Shoe → Hoka Speedgoat 7 (Men’s/Women’s).

Shop Men’s at amazon.com | Shop Women’s at amazon.com.

Recent findings suggest that according to Notary, the two main sacrifices you make when buying cheaper running shoes are comfort and longevity. That doesn’t mean you’re stuck with choosing uncomfortable shoes when you’re searching for cheaper pairs. It just means you have to do the extra, er, footwork, when considering more affordable shoes.

In a recent development, notary notes the materials are not as premium or as durable. “That being said, the industry does benefit from what I call the technology trickle-down; many of the materials on lower priced models were once used on a ‘fancier’ one.” For example, the Brooks Launch 12 has DNA Flash v2 foam which was used in its Hyperion Elite super shoes.

Sources indicate that “A lower cost shoe will use older foams and fabrics, possibly less outsole, or no outsole, and less involved construction techniques. All of those realities typically lead to less overall comfort than what else is at the moment available,” claims Notary. A cheaper shoe will be comfortable, it just won’t have the same max plush and support of a top-shelf trainer.

Sources indicate that notary states comfort is king. “If it feels heavy, stiff, and firm in the store, don’t expect that to change. Conversely, if it feels hyper-light, super flexible, and marshmallowy soft, there is a good chance it won’t be as durable.”.

Perhaps you’re leaning toward one end of the spectrum of cushioning or somewhere in the middle. The best way to find if a cheap shoe—or any running shoe—is right for you is to try it on first and go for a test run in the store. Some shoe stores allow you to run on the sidewalk or on a treadmill to see if the shoe’s a good fit.

Cheap running shoes have a shorter shelf life. “Because the materials are less premium they typically break down faster even when they’re not being worn,” indicates Notary. “This isn’t always true and is somewhat of a generalization, but higher grade materials generally offer more durability. If we’re considering mileage, a lower-cost shoe typically yields fewer miles.”.

Notary adds, however, that some of the most expensive running shoes on the market right now, i.e., super shoes or shoes with a carbon plate, also have a shorter mileage life, which is another thing to put in perspective.

Recent findings suggest that we took pains not to include discounted models on this list but shouldn’t be overlooked when buying running shoes. In some cases, the differences between last season and the current season are unnoticeable.

When the Price Is Too Good to Be True.

Sources indicate that beware of dupes on sites like Amazon. A usually expensive model slapped with a too-good-to-be-true price tag is probably just that. The model in question likely isn’t the shoe promised, is poorly made, and could cause injury due to poor quality materials. Check the seller to see it’s from the actual brand (and make sure it’s not someone posing as a well-known brand).

Sources indicate that for models by lesser known brands, Notary gives us some pointers when choosing running shoes. “Things to look for are a rubber outsole and a removable footbed/liner,” he says. “These are two quick check aspects of a viable running shoe. Also, look for fewer sewn overlays on the upper, more will only cause problems with flexibility and add excessive weight to the shoe.”.

Will cheap running shoes make me run slower?

In a recent development, in general, a cheaper shoe will not have as much pop or energy return as a more expensive one which in theory should make it slower. Lower cost shoes will likely lack plating or supercritical foams found in today’s ‘fastest’ shoes. However, a lot depends on how comfortably the shoe moves with you. Some of the ‘fastest’ shoes on the market today don’t agree with my body’s mechanics, and I find them slower than more conventional shoes in my rotation.

Are cheap running shoes a good choice for new runners?

In a recent development, in my world, any shoe that gets someone running is a good choice. That said, a well-fitting, comfortable technical running shoe will have a much better chance of keeping a latest runner in the sport.

Sources indicate that it’s a shame that with so much great and relatively affordable product available, many people start the sport in the wrong shoe and quit, never knowing a different reality exists for them. Unfortunately the ‘running shoe’ category is a bit of a catch-all, and there are plenty of shoes categorized as ‘running’ that have no place being labeled as such.

How old can a past shoe model be for it to be ok to run in?

Recent findings suggest that unworn shoes will definitely lose some cushioning after about two to five years due to oxidization, which hardens the midsole foam. Glue also weakens over time, increasing the risk of delamination in shoes that have been sitting around a while, primarily between the upper and the midsole and the midsole and the outsole. They can be used, sure, but they won’t have the typical 300 to 500 mile range of usability nor the comfort of a ‘fresher’ pair.

Amanda Furrer, Editor, Running Reviews, studied journalism at NYU and writing at Emerson College. She has reviewed gear and covered other topics in the running space for almost 10 years. Since 2013, she has consecutively run the Boston Marathon. She also has a master’s degree in gastronomy from Boston University and was formerly a professional baker for two years before hanging up her apron.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that we earn a commission for products purchased through some links in this article. Why Trust Us?

Industry observers note that nothing sucks harder on a run than an uncomfortable, unsupportive (or too supportive) sports bra that digs, chafes, causes pools of sweat to collect, and generally makes you curse the day you hit puberty. Luckily, we’re looking out for you. Our team was as rigorous with bras as we are with running shoes, treadmills, and other gear as we evaluated them. We focused chiefly on comfort, breathability, durability, the potential to chafe, bounce control, and ease of laundering.

And yes, we look at bras with and without pads, because anyone who has ever wrestled with those flimsy things can tell you that while they may hide the headlights, there are times when you’d rather light them on fire than deal with them before lacing up and hitting your run.

The best sports bras for running work with your cup and band size, what level of support you require, and how you like it to fit on your frame. We chose a range of adjustable high-impact bras, traditional pullover sports bras, bras with pockets, bras that are budget-friendly, and bras made for different size and shape breasts.

Our testers span all experience levels, paces, ages, and body types, with sizes ranging from 28 to 40 bands and A to F cups. Over the past year, we’ve tested more than 45 different sports bras to see how they held us and how they held up. We wore these bras for running plus low- to high-intensity workouts like yoga and HIIT, evaluating each for comfort, breathability, mobility, and—of course—support.

We sorted our picks into three categories: adjustable bras (hook-and-eye closures, zip fronts, Velcro, or adjustable straps), pullover bras (no adjusting required, though maybe some contorting), and pocket bras, which we also rank on storage space and how packing affects mobility and support.

We upgrade this roundup regularly, but inventory changes fast—some colors and sizes may run low.

Industry observers note that there are few bras that you try on and feel comfortable straight out of the bag, but the Run Times Bra manages. It’s a comfortably compressive, encapsulated, adjustable bra that is designed to take you for long miles. It has sweat-wicking fabric that prevents pooling under the breasts, and the mesh panel at the top allows for additional breathability. On a long run, that extra breeze makes a huge difference in comfort and chafing prevention.

According to recent reports, our tester took this out on a 35-mile climbing trail run through the Adirondack Mountains and through the heat and the rain. The bra performed beautifully, even under a long-sleeve tee and tech jacket. It didn’t get swampy, nor did the shirt start to stick to it, as can happen when sweat and water soak a T-shirt.

Recent findings suggest that it’s especially great for women who have lost a significant amount of breast volume due to weight loss or breastfeeding because of how the additional Lycra material encapsulates and hugs each breast. Where some bras may make these breasts feel almost “folded,” the Run Times Bra simply supports and cradles your breasts in an anatomically comfortable way.

Old Navy has long been a favorite of ours for its inexpensive athletic wear, and now, that also includes sports bras. The PowerSoft bra hits well outside of its weight class in both features and performance, starting with a front zipper that spares you the post-run wrestle of a sweaty pullover. Adjustable cross-back straps let you fix the fit through your shoulders and torso, and the brand’s namesake PowerSoft fabric is buttery soft with moisture-wicking that holds up when you’re hitting those hot runs.

The size range is where Old Navy really indicates up the competition: broader than what many premium brands offer. At $40 full price—and often marked down below $25—it’s impossible to overlook.

And not for anything, this is one of the bras we tested with a zipper that isn’t a sensory nightmare for our autistic testers.

The construction of this bra makes it among the best I’ve ever worn. The uniqueness of that construction? A dual adjustable strap in the back that allows you to dial in your fit. If you need more support up top, you can clasp it closer together. Need a bit more band space? The lower hooks are there for you. This is a bra designed for women who may have volume in different spots across their ribs and chest. And it works beautifully.

It has been revealed that the construction also makes for a more comfortable experience. I have a pretty severe rib flare thanks to pregnancy and a short waist, and the ability to tighten the bra more up on top and less on the bottom makes it comfier than most other bras I’ve tested.

In a recent development, however, if you have pronounced lat muscles, you may notice a bit of rubbing during pull-ups because of where the shoulder straps fall. But that nitpicky aspect doesn’t take away from it being an all-around winner.

Runderwear Power Running Bra Review.

Sources indicate that the Shadowlite is very sensory friendly. The flat-locked seams are coated and stitched in a way that they don’t rub or interfere with your run. It’s also not a traditional encapsulation bra, nor is it a traditional pullover compression bra. Instead, it’s a combination of the two. Instead of the sewn-in lifting panel squeezing the breasts together and in, it lifts them together without the squish.

In a recent development, “The bra gave me a very secure feeling without restricting my breathing—I forgot I was wearing it, which is always the best possible outcome,” said Senior Features Editor Pavlína Černá. “The band has ribbing on the inside that I found helpful in keeping the bra in place—no feeling of rotation on the run. I usually try to get two runs out of a bra, if I can, before washing. I was able to do three with this bra.”.

The gel-cushioned straps on this sports bra ensure you won’t get raw markings from all-day wear and intense activities. The Spot Comfort is also extremely breathable and moisture-wicking—mesh on the adjustable straps and front panel promotes ventilation.

Industry observers note that the bra is lined with molded cups for non-underwire support, and the back hook-and-eye closure makes it easy to take the bra off. One thing to consider: size up. We found the fit a little too snug, even on the loosest hook-and-eye setting. It’s also H-back-only, which may not be everyone’s preference when wearing a sports bra. This one launders like a dream—seriously. For the price, it doesn’t pill, it doesn’t stretch out, and we don’t always follow our own laundering advice and just throw it in with everything and call it good.

In a recent development, the Energy’s foam cups, which go up to size DDD, offer comfortable and secure support while also providing a flattering fit that doesn’t squish the chest down. In the back, we appreciate the crisscross straps’ fun design as well as their functionality—once adjusted, the straps stay in place for a no-budge run.

Some of our testers reported that the Energy runs small, so it may be best to order a size up to ensure the bra is a good fit or try it on in person. This bra also has three points of adjustment: the chest band as well as both sets of cross straps.

The bra that underwent 2,000-plus miles of ultrarunning is buttery soft and has plenty of lift. Tested during lululemon’s Further campaign, in which 10 women runners ran an ultra over the course of six days, the Go Further Bra is a high-impact pullover that can carry you through thousands of miles—and it doesn’t have to be in one go.

The bra is made of lululemon’s Ultralu fabric, which feels yoga legging smooth. Support Code technology in the cups changes the stiffness of the cups to prevent your breasts from bouncing as you run. You can see the tech when the bra is on a flat surface; instead of the conical domes you see on an encapsulation bra, the cups pucker and look slightly sunken in.

According to recent reports, our tester, who wears a 32B and tested the Go Further in a small, had her doubts when she saw the bra lying flat on her desk. She changed her mind after running in the Go Further. “From the look of her, I was convinced that she would never fit, and that she’s made for much bigger boobs than mine,” she says. “And was I wrong! She fits like a glove and is easy to put on and take off. She doesn’t deprive me of air but is completely supportive on my runs.”.

Recent findings suggest that you’ve probably seen influencer ads for this all over your social media feeds. Running Girl’s ad budget is thriving, but thankfully, your budget will be too, if you grab this one. The bra is comfortably high-impact with no squish. Instead, the molded cups lift and separate your breasts doing more holding than straight compression.

Recent findings suggest that the bra is featherlight and breathable but be forewarned, there’s a lot of cup to these cups. I get that it’s an aesthetics thing, but it is wild seeing yourself in a sports bra that adds to your breasts. If you’re not opposed to more boobs than ever on a run (and honestly, it looked good to me!), and you want a simple, affordable bra, this is a great option.

This extremely reasonably priced back-pocket bra is one of my top picks from my sports bras with pocket testing. The phone pocket is easy to reach, and, unlike other pocket bras, there isn’t an overload of material along the back strap design. That does mean the pocket is shallower than similar models, and I find myself reaching back to make sure my phone is still there (I haven’t lost it yet, but it’s something to keep in mind).

This bra is available in a ridiculous array of fun colors, has an easy-to-wear shape, and features a well-fitted design with good coverage and comfort for most cup sizes. For those of us wearing wired headphones, you can thread the cords through a bonded eyelet above the pocket, and the bra stays quite odor resistant even after sweaty workout sessions.

To determine your sports bra size, Lawson uses this system of measuring:.

According to recent reports, but this equation isn’t doctrine. There is no industry standard for bra sizing; not every brand follows the same conventions of measurement. Some brands, for instance, instruct customers to add 4 or 5 inches to the band measurement to determine band size.

“I’ve been creating, evaluating, revising, critiquing sports bra fit charts for decades for brands large and small,” Lawson says. “Because our bodies and breasts are so diverse, it’s virtually impossible for any brand to create the perfect sizing scheme and fit chart that works for 100 percent of women.” But Lawson calls this “a blessing,” comparing sports bras to jeans. Imagine if every size 10 jean had a standardized fit. That would alienate curvier, thinner, shorter, or taller individuals. “It can take trial and error to find your perfect jeans fit match, but once you do it can be a life-changer.” And the same goes for sports bras.

She offers some tips to navigate the Wild West of bra sizing.

When it comes to support, there are two basic sports bra designs: compression and encapsulation. Compression is when strong elastic materials are used to compress your chest. Encapsulation is when each breast is supported separately in its own cup. According to Lawson, many women with larger breasts prefer encapsulation because they find it more comfortable. “It’s not smooshing everything together, trapping moisture between the breasts,” she indicates. That being mentioned, some encapsulation bras, such as the SheFit, Janji, and lululemon Run Times, also offer degrees of compression inside the encapsulation, which serve as both impact protection and an additional layer of support and protection for larger-busted people or those who have lost volume.

Regardless of the type of chest design, an adjustable waistband and shoulder straps help improve overall support when you have larger breasts. More padded straps won’t necessarily translate to a more comfortable fit, Lawson says. Putting in more foam may initially feel more comfortable, but it won’t decrease pressure. “The one thing that will decrease strap pressure is a wider strap. If you make the strap twice as wide, it doesn’t quite cut the shoulder pressure in half, but it’ll take it almost down to half.”.

It has been revealed that some of my favorite racing shorts are pocketless, which isn’t a major deal—when your sports bra has pockets. Some brands offer bras with side pockets and front pockets for housing keys or gels. There are bras with back pockets for storing your smartphone as well. A thing to note with bra storage is that you could be sacrificing support if you weigh down your bra with items.

Some people believe that storing your phone in your bra can increase your breast cancer risk. “There is no conclusive data to suggest that cell phones are linked to cancer,” says Diana Medgyesy, MD, a medical oncologist at UCHealth. However, she adds that “this is an evolving field since cell phone technology and the use of cell phones are changing rapidly,” so use your own discretion on whether or not to run with your phone in your bra.

According to recent reports, when it comes to finding the best sports bra for you, patience and some trial and error are key. “Be prepared to become a sleuth,” Lawson states. “Be prepared to do a little work to understand your own body/breasts and then a lot of work to sleuth out brands whose fit philosophies and metrics match your needs and preferences.

“Most of us are willing to try a dozen or more running shoe brands/styles/sizes to get the best product match for our feet and workouts—give your sports bra quest the same effort and attention to detail.”.

In a recent development, one population of runners we don’t want to leave out is those who have had lumpectomies, mastectomies, or other breast surgeries. That’s why we spoke with breast surgeon and runner Deborah M. Capko, MD, FACS, from Memorial Sloan Kettering in Latest York City. She states that “it’s all about compression” for women who have had breast surgery. For up to a year after surgery, you could be dealing with swelling and discomfort during your runs. Having a compressive bra like a SheFit or lululemon Run Times bra can help.

According to recent reports, capko claims underwires are a no-go, but keeping your post-op breasts “stable and highly supported” can cut down on that swelling and pain. We also spoke with a few runners who have run postmastectomy and lumpectomy, and they agree. When it comes to preferred bra design, they suggested clasp or zip over pullover because a pullover is harder to deal with and far less comfortable.

What is the best sports bra type for running?

Ideally, you want a bra that has a medium or high level of support, a secure, but not too tight band, and straps that sit just before the acromion bone (the boney protuberance at the top of your shoulder.

What Makes a Sports Bra High Impact?

It has been revealed that high-impact sports bras are made to decrease breast movement while you’re performing high-impact activities. They usually use some sort of compression, encapsulated cups, molded cups, supportive fabrics, wider bands, and adjustable straps or closures or combination of these to create a secure fit.

Sources indicate that A running sports bra should feel supportive and pretty darn snug without making you feel like you can’t breathe. The band should sit nicely around your torso, under your breasts, and the cups should fully contain your breasts. The straps shouldn’t slip, and if you’re noticing slipping of any area during your run, it either needs adjustment or you need a upcoming size.

According to recent reports, getting a bra with flat-locked seams like those on this list, with well-fitting straps and the correct cup size is the most key thing. Having good, moisture-wicking fabric allows it to dry faster to prevent friction. Before you head out on a long run, do a shorter workout first to try to notice potential hot spots.

How Often Should You Wash Your Sports Bra?

Sources indicate that you can wear your bra several times before washing, but be sure to wash it at least every couple of runs. Because you’re sweating in the sports bra during running, which is a high-intensity activity, your bra can develop bacteria buildup (gross).

Most sports bras can be tossed into the washing machine, but read the garment label just in case. Refrain from adding in fabric softener, since that can degrade the material and interfere with its breathability and moisture-wicking properties.

According to recent reports, air-drying is strongly recommended, although you can put the bra in the dryer on a tumble setting. Heat from your machine can degrade the bra’s structure as well.

How long does a sports bra last?

According to recent reports, like a running shoe, sports bra shelf life is dependent on the wearer. While it’s recommended you retire your sports bra once or twice a year, we get it—you’ve formed an attachment. But there are telltale signs that it’s time to say goodbye. If the straps are overstretched, the band is loose or causes friction when it never used to, the cups have lost shape, or there’s a hole in the fabric, time for a new bra.

According to recent reports, another sign to go shopping: your body has changed and the bra doesn’t fit like it used to. It’s worth buying a upcoming sports bra that gives you proper support instead of willing an old bra to give you support it can no longer provide.

According to recent reports, bra manufacturers have a real issue creating a full range of sizes for high-impact sports bras. It is rare to find a bra that goes above a 42DDD. SheFit manages, and a few select other brands, but in general, bras with band sizes above 42 and cup sizes above DDD are hard to come by. This is an error in the industry that makes it difficult for people in larger bodies to achieve their running and fitness goals comfortably. Plus-size runners are wildly underrepresented across the span of gear. Running and running gear should be accessible for all, no matter the size of body you live in.

According to recent reports, runner’s World began covering all things running in 1966, but the first sports bra, the Jogbra, wasn’t invented until a decade later. Sports bras are as necessary as a pair of running shoes. Since their invention, they continue to undergo changes in design and tech.

We researched the history of the sports bra and combed through the products available on the market today. We spoke with designers, brand representatives, and experts in the field, including LaJean Lawson, PhD.

Known as Dr. Sports Bra in her field, Lawson has two graduate degrees in sports bra science and is the principal at Creative Fitness Solutions in Portland, Oregon.

Additional interviewing and research was done by Senior Features Editor Pavlína Černá, Deputy Health & Fitness Editor Mallory Creveling, and Director of Hype Aly Ellis.

Tonal Review (2025): Our Experts Put the Smart Home Gym to the Test

📅 29 Jan 2025 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4614 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Breakingmuscle

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that tonal is a high-tech smart gym that makes starting an effective strength workout as easy as stepping into the next room.
  • As a certified personal trainer and wellness product reviewer, I’ve tried (and stopped using) several pieces of home gym equipment.
  • This Tonal review describes our experience using it, including details about the equipment, workouts, accessories, and other features.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that tonal is a high-tech smart gym that makes starting an effective strength workout as easy as stepping into the next room. It has a cable resistance system with multiple attachments, so there is no need for additional equipment. You can choose between instructor-led sessions or work out independently using the demonstrations on the large touchscreen. There are a variety of workouts outside of strength training, including high-intensity interval training (HIIT), cardio, dance, yoga, Pilates, and more.

As a certified personal trainer and wellness product reviewer, I’ve tried (and stopped using) several pieces of home gym equipment. I also work with a team of other expert product reviewers, some of whom have had Tonal for several years and still use it consistently.

This Tonal review describes our experience using it, including details about the equipment, workouts, accessories, and other features. We also spoke to fitness expert Rachael Gonzalez, C.P.T., C.S.C.S., about Tonal’s workout modes and how they can benefit exercisers.

Related: Best Home Gym Equipment.

Based on our experience, we give Tonal an overall 5/5 rating. The only category where it didn’t receive a score is assembly, which doesn’t apply since professional installation is required.

Here’s a look at the scoring breakdown on a scale of 1–5:.

We’re extremely satisfied with the Tonal equipment and programming. We can get a full workout without taking up a lot of space with free weights or having to pay to go to a gym and leave the house.

In a recent development, the equipment is durable, and we haven’t had any issues. However, moving the arms can be noisy, which may concern people installing it on a shared wall. We had one arm that clicked slightly for a while, but following the troubleshooting instructions on the Tonal website helped fix it.

According to recent reports, some weightlifting moves don’t feel entirely safe or stable, so we usually replace them with ones we’re more comfortable with. The handles, bar, and rope accessories are comfortable to hold and easy to use.

According to recent reports, tonal automatically adjusts weight as you progress, which is really nice. Some workouts have a movement replacement option where you select a modification for the recommended exercise, which has been helpful in certain instances. For example, during pregnancy, you’re supposed to avoid twisting moves, so when one of our testers started lifting after her first trimester, she could easily substitute these moves.

In a recent development, tonal has worked very well, and one of our testers indicates it has drastically improved her strength. When she started using Tonal in 2021, she was in the bottom 25 percent of all women. Now, she’s in the top 28 percent, and watching her score increase has motivated her to keep improving.

Recent findings suggest that the Tonal machine is a wall-mounted smart mirror with a built-in touchscreen and two adjustable arms that extend from the sides of the machine and can be moved up and down depending on what exercises you’re doing. You can choose between an on-demand or live instructor-led class or do your own exercises using the Free Lift option. Throughout each class and in Free Lift mode, a trainer explains how to adjust the arms and attach accessories and demonstrates proper form.

Workouts on the built-in workout app include weightlifting exercises such as squats, deadlifts, shoulder presses, lat pulldowns, tricep extensions, curls, and bench presses. The movement library has over 170 exercises to choose from. Each exercise is performed under the resistance of a cable pulley system using a bar, rope, or handle attachment, with up to 100 pounds of resistance per side for a combined 200 pounds.

Related: Best Functional Trainers.

Tonal recommends weights for each session based on an initial assessment, and your progress and performance determine adjustments. It offers unique weight modes, video form feedback, and floor workouts such as yoga and Pilates. The Tonal app also gives you access to workouts that don’t require the machine arms, so you can work out on the go.

Sources indicate that tonal uses artificial intelligence—Coach AI—to track progress, movement, and data from your workouts to make adjustments, weight recommendations, program suggestions, and more. You don’t have to worry about answering questions like: What do I need to work on today? What weights should I use? Should I focus on my lower body or do a full-body workout? Instead, one tap of the 24-inch touchscreen reveals an interactive library of on-demand and live classes or workout programs. Even in Free Lift mode, an option often used by experienced lifters, Coach AI tracks your data and makes adjustments and weight recommendations.

The first time you use Tonal, you’ll complete the Strength Assessment, which starts by choosing from the following goals:.

After selecting your goal, you’ll indicate whether you are a beginner, intermediate, or advanced exerciser and perform several movements—including a seated lat pulldown, seated overhead press, bench press, and neutral grip deadlifts—to help Coach AI get to know you and adapt to your needs, much like an online personal trainer. Your strength assessment results are used by Coach AI as a baseline when selecting the weight for each movement and to recommend workouts and programs.

It has been revealed that while this is a good starting point, it could be better. It’s hard to assess your overall fitness based on a single workout—what if you had an off day? Tonal addresses this by learning more about your strength level based on your performance in subsequent workouts and adjusting the weight settings to reflect your strength better.

During daily training sessions, it uses metrics such as time under tension, power output, range of motion, weight, and time to make weight adjustments and measure progress. Coach AI can detect when your form isn’t correct using your positioning, range of motion, and pacing. If it senses uncertain quality, it provides audible and on-screen reminders and feedback or turns off the weight. For example, the resistance shuts off if the bar tilts during a bench press because it suggests the movement is incorrect or unstable. If it senses you are moving the weight too easily, it increases the load each rep so you get the intended stimulus of the workout.

Recent findings suggest that another impressive feature is the four weight modes: Spotter, Burnout, Chains, and Eccentric. In Spotter mode, Tonal senses when you are struggling with a rep, lowers the weight so you can complete it, and returns the weight for the next rep to re-challenge your strength. Burnout senses fatigue and reduces weight until you finish the set. The Chains mode replicates the feeling of putting chains on the barbell by increasing the resistance during a lift’s concentric or shortening phase. Eccentric increases the resistance as you release the weight for more time under tension, which may help muscle growth.

It has been revealed that tonal enables each mode automatically during live and on-demand workouts. This automation creates a seamless transition between segments like supersets, where you concentrate on opposing muscle groups with little rest in between. If you want to work out with a partner, weight adjustments for both parties are automated.

Sources indicate that experienced experts lead each workout by demonstrating and talking you through set up and proper form. Even if you choose to follow the Free Lift setting or build a custom workout using the extensive movement library, there are video explanations of how to perform each movement. When you enable a specific weight mode, the weight is adjusted automatically, or you can adjust it manually on the screen using the dial. Interestingly, you can adjust the weight in one-pound increments, an uncommon feature in most cable machines and free weights, which typically adjust in 2.5 or five-pound increments.

Recent findings suggest that to access these features, you’ll need a paid membership for $60 monthly, and Tonal requires a subscription for the first year. The only way to use Tonal without the membership is to manually set the weights to perform unguided exercises like a cable machine.

According to recent reports, the purchase price of $3,995 includes the machine (which includes the touchscreen and arms) and no accessories. Aside from the floor workouts, most workouts use the arms and attachments, so Tonal isn’t usable without them. While you can use attachments from other brands, you’ll need to purchase T-lock adapters from Tonal for $43.

The smart accessories bundle from Tonal costs $495. If your budget allows, I recommend buying it because it includes everything you need to start using your Tonal immediately. Each accessory is available separately, so you can also choose what works best for you. Here’s a breakdown of what the bundle includes and pricing for each item individually:.

Recent findings suggest that the smart accessories have a safety feature to turn the weight on and off with a button rather than by touching the screen, so you can position yourself before loading. The handles have a button on the side that’s easy to reach while gripping, and the rope and bar come with an attachable clip.

According to recent reports, as a beginner, our tester initially thought working out with Tonal was intimidating, but it’s a simple process once you learn how the smart home gym works. With a membership, you can choose between live and on-demand classes or a progressive program. Based on your Strength Score established in the initial assessment, the recommended weights are set automatically for you.

From there, you follow the trainer’s instructions and on-screen prompts to set the arms and choose the right accessories for each move. Tonal automatically adjusts the weight, counts reps, and provides form feedback as you progress through the workout. There’s even an audible cue when you have two reps left, so you know what to expect if you’re facing away from the machine.

Free Lift allows you to choose from the library of movements and do as many sets and reps as you’d like. Much like the classes, the screen displays your live stats, and you receive a workout summary with your time under tension, range of motion, power output, and total volume lifted.

You can do floor workouts such as cardio, yoga, and barre directly on Tonal or by using the Tonal app on another device.

Industry observers note that strength training is the main draw of Tonal, so most of Tonal’s content focuses on weightlifting and HIIT training with weights. In addition to the four weight modes mentioned earlier, there are two custom modes:.

In a recent development, gonzalez claims these options add variety and challenge, enhancing strength gains and training overall. “Diversification in your routine keeps you engaged and introduces upcoming challenges,” she says. “Plus, variation can help you push past a training plateau.”.

Sources indicate that trainer-led workouts on Tonal automatically implement these modes depending on the intended stimuli, but you can activate them manually in the settings for any workout. You can adjust the weight at any point during your workout using the dial on the screen.

According to recent reports, “When training, I’m always super mindful of how my body feels and take it easy when I need to, so the Recovery Mode option would work well for when you’re sore or just want to move,” Gonzalez states. “I really like the eccentric-focused mode. During the eccentric portion of a rep, the muscle lengthens while under tension,” she says. “The eccentric portion of a lift occurs when you are lowering the weight, moving against the opposing force of gravity, and research reveals controlled lengthening of the muscle fibers contributes to overall strength and muscle development.”.

In addition, there are several other types of workouts available on Tonal, including:.

Tonal has a massive catalog of guided workouts and workout programs and a library of over 200 bodyweight moves to allow you to build custom workouts.

The guided programs range from three to five weeks and focus on goals like improving overall fitness, gaining lean muscle mass, and burning fat. For example, Fundamentally Fit guides you through basic movement patterns, and House of Volume uses progressive overload to build strength. Many consumers on Reddit recommend Four Weeks to Fat Loss, a combination of resistance training and HIIT to maximize energy output. One indicates, “Four Weeks to Fat Loss did amazing things to my body composition! Doing that program was when I really started to see a difference in how my clothes fit.”.

The smart handles help replicate moves performed with dumbbells and kettlebells, like hammer curls, bicep curls, or goblet squats. The smart rope can copy moves with a rope or chains, like pull-throughs or tricep extensions. Finally, the bar can replicate barbell moves such as deadlifts and bench presses. You can purchase accessories from another brand, but the smart accessories bundle from Tonal has Bluetooth connectivity, so you can press a single button on the accessory to turn the weight on or off.

If you buy third-party accessories, you must purchase T-locks from Tonal to attach them securely. Additionally, you’ll need to turn the weight on and off directly on the touchscreen.

Tonal has a roster of expert instructors based in its New York studio and guest coaches who occasionally provide unique content. These fitness experts have diverse backgrounds, from competitive athletes to sports medicine.

All Tonal-created workouts are instructor-led, so you’ll hear tips about form and safety throughout. Each instructor brings a unique style, personality, and expertise to the table, and Tonal users generally find instructors they prefer. For many, this provides the experience of working with a personal trainer, and several of Tonal’s past and current coaches offer personal training services outside of Tonal. For these reasons, Tonal allows you to filter workouts by instructor.

It has been revealed that the Tonal app allows you to access your workout history, create workouts, and do floor workouts directly from your phone. The only thing you can’t do on the Tonal app is weightlifting workouts that require using the resistance cables.

In addition, Tonal connects to several fitness apps, including Apple Health, Google Fit, and Strava. It also syncs with several heart rate monitors using Bluetooth, and you can connect to your Amazon Music or Apple Music account to stream or choose from the 14 stations on Tonal Radio.

Tonal has several features to help keep members engaged with the community and the equipment.

First, there are several achievements you can earn for performing certain types of workouts, working out on holidays or birthdays, or reaching milestones like weekly streaks or 1,000,000 pounds lifted. Your workout summary lists the badges and milestones reached and your progress toward the following milestones. The Total Achievements Card shows how many workouts you’ve finished, the pounds you’ve lifted, and the longest weekly streak you’ve completed. You earn badges by trying a new workout type, training consistently, and working out at a different time of day. These achievements can be shared with friends and family using the mobile app.

The Tonal Leaderboard ranks all active exercisers based on how many days or hours they’ve used Tonal in the last 30 days, so the more you train, the higher you’ll rank.

Your Strength Score increases from the baseline as you get stronger and demonstrate progress during workouts. These improvements are calculated based on your historical workout data and are a huge source of motivation for many Tonal users. Using a percentage-based comparison, you can see how your Strength Score ranks against others, so some friendly competition is involved.

Tonal has a very active social media community if you prefer direct interaction with other members. The brand’s private Facebook community, The Official Tonal Community (OTC), has over 53,000 members and regularly hosts workout challenges and live discussions with Tonal trainers.

Our tester has had Tonal for over two years, and she’s used it consistently the entire time, only stepping away briefly for injury recovery and pregnancy.

Before Tonal, despite being fully aware of the benefits of resistance training, she had no weightlifting experience beyond the occasional half-hearted kettlebell or dumbbell workout.

Recent findings suggest that tonal takes all the guesswork out of resistance training so you can lift the weights and reap the benefits, which is our favorite thing about it. You don’t have to worry about setting weights, planning workouts, increasing weights or reps, or tracking your progress.

At first, our tester didn’t understand Tonal’s difficulty levels. Beginner classes may include heavy weights if recommended by your Strength Score and the algorithm. In a recent development, our tester says Tonal is a lot of fun. She’s discovered she loves lifting weights, and when she misses a few workouts, she gets antsy about getting started again. Sometimes, she struggles with the pacing for floor/cardio workouts but finds the weightlifting workouts easy to follow. Mostly, she sticks to on-demand workouts because she appreciates the guided warm-up, exercise, and cool-down.

Recent findings suggest that one concern users in the Tonal Facebook community raise is the lead trainer demonstrates the moves during a live workout, which is not true for on-demand classes. These workouts use the lead trainer’s voiceover and cut to another trainer demonstrating the exercises. This inconsistency doesn’t bother us, but some say it disrupts their flow or makes it harder to follow.

The instructors showcase their personalities, and none of the workouts our tester watched seem overly scripted or cheesy. Our reviewer had grown accustomed to the “old” coaches and still gravitates toward their workouts because she likes their calm demeanor. In a recent development, these trainers have diverse professional backgrounds to support the workouts they design. For example, when our tester’s doctor cleared her to work out after a knee injury, she found Coach Liz’s workouts helpful because the coach is also a physical therapist.

Sources indicate that our tester completed several of the guided programs and saw consistent strength gains from each program. The programs can get repetitive, though, since many of them repeat the same two or three workouts for the duration of the program.

According to recent reports, when our tester started using Tonal, her Strength Score was 133, and she was in one of the lowest percentiles of all female Tonal members. The collegiate fall racing calendar isn't quite finished, with the 2026 NCAA Cross Country National Championships bringing together teams and individual athletes looking to end their seasons with a title.

It has been revealed that division I gets underway Saturday, November 21, in Terre Haute, Indiana, where 32 men's teams and 32 women's teams will compete. Alongside them will be 38 individual qualifiers whose schools didn't make the team field.

It has been revealed that if you've been keeping a close eye on college cross country this season, there's plenty to be excited about this weekend. Oklahoma State returns as the defending men's team champion and winners of two of the past three titles, while NC State's women will look to add another trophy to a particularly successful stretch of their own, having collected four championships since 2021.

Fortunately, you don't have to make the trip to Indiana to catch the action. Here's when everything starts, where the races are being held, and how to watch from home.

The Division I and Division III championships will both take place on Saturday, November 21, although the two competitions will be held in different states.

Division II runners will have to wait a little longer, with their national championship scheduled for Friday, December 4.

According to the NCAA's championship schedule, here's where each division will compete:.

It has been revealed that for Division I, ESPNU and the ESPN app will carry the national championships live on Saturday, November 21, with coverage beginning at 10 a.m. ET.

The women's 6K starts at 10:20 a.m., followed by the men's 10K at 11:10 a.m., and the trophy presentation scheduled for around noon.

Fans following Divisions II and III can watch their respective competitions through the NCAA.com's live streaming schedule.

Oklahoma State has been tough to beat in recent years, finishing near the top of the men’s standings more often than not. The Cowboys have claimed two of the last five national titles, winning the national title in 2025, with 57 points, 25 points ahead of runner-up Latest Mexico.

Sources indicate that NC State’s women have enjoyed a similarly strong run, having won three straight titles from 2021 to 2023, before BYU took the 2024 championship. NC State reclaimed the top spot last year, with 114 points.

Division I's national field includes 32 teams per gender, with 18 earning automatic spots through the nine regional championships and another 14 receiving bids through an at-large selection process.

There are also 38 individual qualifiers in each race, representing schools that didn't advance as teams, so the competition for the individual titles extends well beyond the athletes wearing jerseys from the leading programs. With both individual and team titles on the line, there's plenty to follow once the starting gun goes off.

U.S. Women Could Be Upgraded to World Half Marathon Gold After Kenyan Runner’s EPO Ban

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (507 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Runnersworld

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Emma Grace Hurley, Weini Kelati, and Jess McClain already had plenty to celebrate after earning the United States its first women's team medal at September's World Road Running Championships in Copenhagen.
  • On Thursday, November 19, the Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) declared that Kenya's Veronica Loleo had received a three-year doping ban after testing positive for erythropoietin (EPO), a prohibited substance.
  • The Kenyan women originally led with a combined 3:17:33, ahead of the Americans' 3:19:51.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Emma Grace Hurley, Weini Kelati, and Jess McClain already had plenty to celebrate after earning the United States its first women's team medal at September's World Road Running Championships in Copenhagen. But nearly two months after finishing with silver, the American trio could soon have gold added to their résumés.

On Thursday, November 19, the Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) declared that Kenya's Veronica Loleo had received a three-year doping ban after testing positive for erythropoietin (EPO), a prohibited substance. The decision officially disqualifies her second-place finish at the September 20 event, where her silver medal helped Kenya secure the women's team title. But with Loleo's result now thrown out, Kenya's team score has to be recalculated. Countries are ranked by the combined finishing times of their three fastest athletes, and Loleo’s removal means Kenya must now count Lilian Kasait Rengeruk, who finished 34th in 1:10:36, potentially lifting the U.S. to first place in the team standings.

The Kenyan women originally led with a combined 3:17:33, ahead of the Americans' 3:19:51. But removing Loleo's 1:06:05 pushes Kenya's total to 3:22:04, leaving the U.S. in first place by two minutes and 13 seconds. Kenya would drop to second and Ethiopia would remain third, although World Athletics has yet to officially confirm the updated results.

Hurley recently acknowledged the uncertainty in a comment on Citius Mag's Instagram, noting that nobody can know exactly how the race would've unfolded without Loleo. Still, she admitted, "it would've been so cool to celebrate gold 🥹.".

Loleo's sample was collected during an out-of-competition test on September 6 ahead of the championships, two weeks prior to the competition. She initially told investigators she couldn't explain the positive result, mentioning an injection she'd received for an injury, but later admitted to the violation on October 30, which earned her a one-year reduction from the standard four-year suspension.

Recent findings suggest that loleo wasn't the only major Kenyan distance runner to receive a final decision Thursday. Peres Jepchirchir, the reigning world marathon champion and 2021 Olympic gold medalist, was also handed a three-year ban following an EPO finding.

“The Kenyan authorities have made a lot of progress in the fight against doping in the last five years, but these cases highlight that there is still a long way to go,” AIU chief executive Brett Clothier remarked in a statement.

“The Kenyan government is aware of the current situation and has committed to further strengthen the Anti-Doping Agency of Kenya and take action to address the criminal networks that facilitate doping within the country.”.

Jepchirchir, who had been provisionally suspended in October, has accepted the disqualification of her results dating back to July 17, including her August victory at the Sydney Marathon. Fellow Kenyan Irine Cheptai is expected to inherit that title.

#171240. This Mileage Target Can Help You Determine Whether You Built a Strong Enough Base to Start Race Training

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (725 w)

This Mileage Target Can Help You Determine Whether You Built a Strong Enough Base to Start Race Training

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (725 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Runnersworld

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Base training involves spending a few weeks running at an easy pace and slowly increasing your mileage over time.
  • According to recent reports, building a sufficient aerobic base helps you avoid the aches and pains that come with ramping up mileage too quickly, especially if you’ve been running sporadically or took some time off.
  • It has been revealed that the hard part of this foundational phase?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Base training involves spending a few weeks running at an easy pace and slowly increasing your mileage over time. It’s a crucial first step in any running journey, designed to help you ease into race-specific training.

According to recent reports, building a sufficient aerobic base helps you avoid the aches and pains that come with ramping up mileage too quickly, especially if you’ve been running sporadically or took some time off. It also makes running feel more doable, as it bridges the gap between your current routine and your goal training plan.

It has been revealed that the hard part of this foundational phase? Figuring out if you’re ready to tackle the first few weeks of a blueprint and start race-specific workouts. Thankfully, coaches offer a helpful benchmark to hit, plus they explain how to smoothly transition your base routine to race training, without shocking your system.

Building a strong base before racing any distance helps prevent injuries and improves long-term performance, including improved aerobic capacity, endurance, faster recovery, mental conditioning, and weight and stress management, Jill Becker, a personal trainer and run coach at Life Time in Westminster, CO, previously told Runner’s World. That’s why the phase is necessary for all runners, whether you’re latest to the sport or have a Boston qualifying time on the list of goals.

“Even a 5K race relies heavily on aerobic systems for energy production—so the better the aerobic base you have, the faster you can race,” Laura Norris, owner and coach at Laura Norris Running in Boulder, CO, previously told Runner’s World.

Additionally, Norris states doing these easy miles weeks before your goal training block allows your body to adapt to the mileage first, so you can then add in speedwork leading up to race day with lower risk of injury and burnout. Taking this approach helps you avoid increasing volume and intensity at the same time, which can often lead to overtraining.

Finally, tackling a base phase means you’ll feel more confident heading into, say, a four-miler with faster-paced efforts (like tempo or race pace miles), as you’ll have already run four miles at an easy pace consistently for several weeks.

Building a strong base requires covering a certain number of miles consistently over the course of several weeks. Beginners should aim to spend at least 10 weeks on this training block, while intermediate runners can follow a six-week proposal, and more advanced runners typically need about four weeks to set that aerobic foundation, Becker notes.

It has been revealed that if you’ve already picked out your training blueprint, Norris recommends working up to at least 80 percent of the weekly mileage prescribed in the first week of that plan. For example, our 20-week beginner marathon plan prescribes 12 miles in the first week. That means you’ll want to work up to about 10 miles per week before diving into the plan. If you’re looking to break two hours in the half marathon, which requires running at least 18 miles in the first week of the Runner’s World plan, then you’ll want to work up to about 15 miles.

According to recent reports, if you haven’t identified your training strategy yet, Becker recommends adding at least 10 miles to your current weekly volume. (If you’re currently running 10 miles a week, work up to 20.).

Look for a strategy that builds up to that mileage goal slowly, following the 10 percent rule, which means increasing your mileage by no more than 10 percent each week.

Keep in mind, base training is about setting the foundation for your next training block, and a part of that process should include recovery time. This means making time for rest days and down weeks (in which you reduce your volume to allow for recovery and better performance), as well as staying on top of your nutrition, sleep habits, and cross-training.
